rows.check: 2.1-citations (attribution, scope, locator), 2.3-grades (T)
rows.location: course/modules/S/S7/L01.html line 436 (interpretation paragraph, span data-cite=koning2026anytime, now data-grade=T)
rows.evidence: Re-checked from scratch. (1) arXiv 2501.03982 v5 (Koning and van Meer, 'Anytime Validity is Free: Inducing Sequential Tests'; curl https://arxiv.org/pdf/2501.03982v5, 510221 bytes, pdftotext -layout): Section 2.2 'Simple hypotheses' states Theorem 1: (1) if phi is valid then (phi_n) is anytime valid; (2) if phi is not valid then phi_tau is not valid for any tau; (3) if phi is F_tau-measurable then phi_tau = phi. Appendix B.1 'Proof of Theorem 1' proves claim 1 by optional stopping for the bounded martingale phi_n = E_P[phi | F_n] (phi_n in [0,1]) and claim 3 directly. (2) The span's 'simple null' scope is Section 2.2 (H = {P}); the composite case is Section 2.3 (Theorem 2). (3) Crossref record of 10.1093/jrsssb/qkag050 (curl api.crossref.org, fetched this round): abstract: 'Given a maximum number of observations N ... for any valid test based on N observations, we show how to construct an anytime valid sequential test that matches it after N observations.' The span restates it for a simple null with N fixed in advance. (4) Grade T: BLUEPRINT §3 allows T for a theorem with a precisely cited proof; the citation (Theorem 1, claims 1 and 3, Section 2.2, Appendix B.1) is precise. The published JRSS-B 88(4) version could not be read (DOI and academic.oup.com return HTTP 403 to curl), so its numbering is unverified; see registry_flags.

rows.evidence: Card: 'Misconception: A t-statistic above 3 proves the predictor is real.' Back: 'With a 99% prior probability of the null, t = 3 still leaves the null more likely than not (Lab 3).' L06.html Section 4 (h2 id s4, line 247) contains Theorem 4.2 (T): Prob(H0|z) >= PO e^(-z^2/2) / (1 + PO e^(-z^2/2)) (equation 4), with PO = 99 and z = 3: e^(-4.5) = 0.011109, x = 99 x 0.011109 = 1.099791, x/(1+x) = 0.523762 > 0.5. The basis is the theorem on the page (T). The claim is the theorem's lower bound, so 'more likely than not' follows. PASS.

(3) PRDS: Proposition 5.3 (L03.html line 281-282) covers z_j = sqrt(rho) W + sqrt(1-rho) eps_j + mu_j with rho in [0,1) and p_j = 1 - Phi(z_j): PRDS on every subset. The Lab 5 twin draws z = sqrt(rho) w + sqrt(1-rho) e + mu (tests/labs/S7/lab-S7-L05-5.py line 39), with mu = 0 on the 450 nulls, so the null p-values are exactly that model. Super-uniformity holds with equality (p = 1 - Phi(z), z ~ N(0,1) under the null; scipy KS vs uniform p = 0.86, 0.57, 0.82 for rho = 0, 0.5, 0.8: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-quant-phd/cdd15252-4236-59f9-8fa8-e63e41e1dc0d/scratchpad/verify23h-data-tooling/out/simes_check_r14.txt). (4) Theorem 5.2 with family size m0 and q = alpha gives FDR <= m0 alpha/m0 = alpha. (5) With all nulls true, V = R, so FDR = E[R/max(R,1)] = P(R >= 1). (6) BH rejects at least one exactly when some q_(l) <= l alpha/m0 (step-up rule), so P(R >= 1) = P(union over l <= m0 of {q_(l) <= l alpha/m0}), the Simes event. Hence the Simes inequality holds for these p-values. (7) By Theorem 7.5 (course/modules/S/S7/L05.html line 560-564): the event {FDP > gamma} is contained in the union over l <= M <= m0, so P(FDP > gamma) <= alpha for constants (3) at every rho in [0,1). rows.location: tools/fetch_data.py _invert (lines 203-222 at 7254468); domain: _PLAIN_NUMBER = -?[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)? (line 141)
rows.evidence: unchanged since 4051c1a (git diff checked); round-23 evidence: Derivation checked line by line. x = Fraction(value), exact; x = 0 is refused (DataError). inv = 1/|x| = q/p exactly, with p = numerator, q = denominator of |x|. lead0 = len(str(q)) - len(str(p)); if q in [10^(n1-1), 10^n1) and p in [10^(n2-1), 10^n2) then inv in (10^(n1-n2-1), 10^(n1-n2+1)), so floor(log10 inv) is lead0-1 or lead0. Output Decimal(digits).scaleb(lead-7) is exact and plain (:f). Sign: the sign of x is restored; abs() makes lead well defined for negative x. Domain: every accepted value is a terminating decimal, so the only inputs whose inverse is an exact 9-digit tie are x = 0.4096 x 10^-k (the ties 2.44140625 x 10^k), as shown in r16-equiv-I03.
